newsitem.title: USA: U.S. priest allegedly stole church funds for lover.
newsitem.headline: U.S. priest allegedly stole church funds for lover.

text.p: A Florida priest has been released on his own recognisance after appearing in court on a charge of grand theft for stealing church money to buy the silence of his homosexual lover, officials said on Friday.

The Rev. Simeon Gardner, 70, a priest for 42 years, retired in August amid allegations that he stole at least $250,000 from St. Mary's Catholic Church in Lutz, Florida, between 1993 and 1996 to buy the silence of a man with whom he had had a homosexual relationship.
His appearance in court on Thursday came after he turned himself in, Assistant State Attorney Anthony Arena said. "It was a voluntary turn-in on one count of first-degree grand theft," he said.
The St. Petersburg Times said Gardner told investigators he used the money to pay off Joseph Mondeau, 36, a bait shop owner from Odessa, Florida, who had threatened to make their relationship public.
Arena said Mondeau had not been charged with any crime. "We are evaluating his conduct in relation to the thefts of money from the church and we are investigating that," he said.

At a bail hearing on Thursday, acting Circuit Judge Walter Heinrich asked Gardner if he "promised before God" to make all court dates in the matter. "You miss any court dates, you'll be in violation of my order, not to mention a higher authority than I," the judge said.
A spokesman for the Archdiocese of St. Petersburg said on Friday that church officials were "saddened by this whole affair" but the church was not commenting further while the matter was in court.
